page: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at a sustained clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features an extensive CPU cache subsystem comprising 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 480 MB L3 cache. Compute capabilities are augmented by hardware instruction flags including AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix operations, and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography.

The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 system memory rated at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local persistent disk storage is not bundled, requiring instances to utilize external block storage services over the network. Networking baseline bandwidth is rated at 15 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this server configuration.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong execution in single-core and multi-threaded throughput. Geekbench scores reach 2187.0 in single-core and 18229.0 in multi-core metrics, with text processing and image processing ranking within top percentiles. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 227.98 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 34.25 GB/sec. In cryptographic operations, PassMark encryption achieves 36252.74, reflecting hardware vector and cipher extensions. Machine learning inference on smaller language models (135M) generates 357.67 tokens/sec, while larger models demonstrate moderate execution speeds typical of purely CPU-bound architectures.

From an engineering perspective, the 2:1 memory-to-core ratio maximizes CPU throughput per unit of memory overhead. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage necessitates factoring in network storage latency for disk-bound tasks. Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is best deployed for high-throughput batch computing, distributed CI/CD build pipelines, web serving clusters, cryptographic microservices, and CPU-driven mathematical modeling.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for compute-heavy workloads. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. System memory comprises 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, establishing a 2.0 GB per core allocation characteristic of compute-focused platforms. The instance bundles no local disk storage, relying on external network volumes over a 15 Gbps baseline link, and features no dedicated GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong performance in cryptographic processing, text analysis, and data compression, alongside capable CPU-based machine learning inference. With high clock frequencies and modern vector extensions, c8i.8xlarge provides balanced cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks, making it suited for batch processing, web serving, and CI/CD pipelines.
